instruments.title: Add KAS, the Estonian Credit Institutions Act (Krediidiasutuste seadus)
instruments.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krediidiasutuste seadus (KAS), RT I 1999, 23, 349, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 16, in force from 01.10.2026 to 30.06.2028, read through the gazette's own interface; entry into force read in § 142 of the act

titles.en: Credit Institutions Act

payload.implementsNote: Financial Conglomerates Directive, Directive 2002/87/EC; CRD, Directive 2013/36/EU, as amended up to CRD6, Directive (EU) 2024/1619, and the EMIR 3 Directive, Directive (EU) 2024/2994; BRRD, Directive 2014/59/EU (the directives the act's footnote in Riigi Teataja lists)

obligations.title: Add the duty: Ensure managers are fit and proper and assess their suitability
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krediidiasutuste seadus (RT I 1999, 23, 349), § 48 lg 2, 2⁴ ja 5², consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 16, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Ensure managers are fit and proper and assess their suitability

summaries.en: A credit institution must ensure that the members of its supervisory board and management board have the knowledge, skills, experience, education, professional suitability and impeccable business reputation needed to manage it. It checks and answers for their meeting the requirements at all times through its own documented suitability assessment, made before they are elected, when new facts come to light and regularly after that. The same holds for a financial holding company or mixed financial holding company approved under § 13⁶.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Notify Finantsinspektsioon before appointing managers and key persons
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krediidiasutuste seadus (RT I 1999, 23, 349), § 48¹ lg 1–3 ja 7, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 16, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Notify Finantsinspektsioon before appointing managers and key persons

summaries.en: A credit institution must tell Finantsinspektsioon of its intention to elect or appoint a manager or key person, or to extend a term of office, at least ten days before the decision, with the data and documents the section lists; a significant credit institution does so at least 30 working days before a manager takes up the post. It must report without delay new facts that may affect a manager's or key person's suitability. It gives at least ten days' notice of a resignation or of starting a removal before the term ends.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep variable pay within fixed pay unless the general meeting approves up to 200 per cent
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krediidiasutuste seadus (RT I 1999, 23, 349), § 57² lg 2 p 1 ja lg 2¹, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 16, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Keep variable pay within fixed pay unless the general meeting approves up to 200 per cent

summaries.en: The variable remuneration of a manager, or of an employee the pay rules cover under § 57¹ lg 3, may not exceed the fixed remuneration. The general meeting may allow up to 200 per cent of fixed pay if the reasoned proposal was on the agenda and sent with the notice of the meeting, at least 66 per cent of the votes represented are in favour, and the institution informs Finantsinspektsioon without delay of the proposal and of the decision. Under § 57¹ lg 2 the rule is followed in full or in part as far as that is proportionate to the nature, scale and complexity of the business.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Run a permanent internal control system with independent audit, risk control and compliance functions
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krediidiasutuste seadus (RT I 1999, 23, 349), § 59 lg 1–5, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 16, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Run a permanent internal control system with independent audit, risk control and compliance functions

summaries.en: A credit institution and each company in its consolidation group must have an internal control system working at all times, proportionate to the nature, scale and complexity of the business and covering every level of management and operations. It consists of internal audit, risk control and compliance functions that are organisationally independent of risk-taking and separate from it. Internal audit may not be combined with any other business line or control function.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Assess internal capital and liquidity adequacy and report on it once a year
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krediidiasutuste seadus (RT I 1999, 23, 349), § 63¹ lg 1, 1¹, 2, 5 ja 6, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 16, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Assess internal capital and liquidity adequacy and report on it once a year

summaries.en: A credit institution must have sound, effective and comprehensive strategies and procedures to keep adequate own funds and liquidity buffers for the risks it takes or may take, hold enough internal capital for all its risks and for the losses that stress tests and scenario analysis show, and have sufficient liquidity at all times. Once a year it submits to Finantsinspektsioon an overview of its internal capital and liquidity adequacy assessment process, drawn up as at the end of the financial year and filed within three months of it, unless Finantsinspektsioon sets another frequency or date.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep group-wide risk strategies and a tested business continuity plan
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krediidiasutuste seadus (RT I 1999, 23, 349), § 82 lg 1, 2, 2² ja 5, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 16, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Keep group-wide risk strategies and a tested business continuity plan

summaries.en: A credit institution and the companies in its consolidation group may not take risks that could endanger their solvency, and must have uniform strategies, procedures and systems for identifying, measuring and managing risk that are proportionate, set out in internal rules and regularly reviewed and updated. The supervisory board and the risk committee receive regular reports on all current and potential risks. The institution must draw up a business continuity plan for all material business processes and regularly review, test and update it.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Lend responsibly and keep data on each client's financial obligations
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krediidiasutuste seadus (RT I 1999, 23, 349), § 83 lg 3, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 16, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Lend responsibly and keep data on each client's financial obligations

summaries.en: When granting and monitoring loans a credit institution must follow its internal credit principles, good banking practice and the principle of responsible lending. To apply that principle it must collect and keep data on the size of the client's financial obligations and on how payment obligations have been met, and use the data to calculate a reasonable debt burden for the client.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Lend to related persons only by unanimous management board decision and on ordinary terms
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krediidiasutuste seadus (RT I 1999, 23, 349), § 84 lg 1–6, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 16, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Lend to related persons only by unanimous management board decision and on ordinary terms

summaries.en: A loan to a person related to the credit institution (its managers, their spouses, registered partners, children and parents and the companies tied to them, and the holders of a qualifying holding the section names) needs a unanimous decision of the management board each time, unless the amount is below 25 per cent of the annual pay of the chair of the management board or a lower threshold set by the supervisory board. The person concerned may not take part in the decision, and the terms may not be more favourable than for others of the same creditworthiness and collateral. The documentation must be available to Finantsinspektsioon on request.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep banking secrecy and disclose client data only on a statutory ground
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krediidiasutuste seadus (RT I 1999, 23, 349), § 88 lg 1, 3, 4 ja 5, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 16, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Keep banking secrecy and disclose client data only on a statutory ground

summaries.en: All data and assessments that a credit institution has learned about its own or another credit institution's client are banking secrecy, which shareholders, managers, employees and others with access must keep without limit in time. The institution may disclose it to a third party only where the section gives a right or duty to do so, the client has consented, or disclosure is needed to perform or prepare a contract with the client. It must disclose it to the authorities the section lists, such as the courts, investigating bodies, the tax authority and bailiffs, in reply to an enquiry made in writing, electronically or through the enforcement register.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Provide basic payment services unless Finantsinspektsioon has released the bank
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krediidiasutuste seadus (RT I 1999, 23, 349), § 88¹ lg 1, 2 ja 6, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 16, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Provide basic payment services unless Finantsinspektsioon has released the bank

summaries.en: A credit institution and the Estonian branch of a foreign credit institution must provide the basic payment services named in § 709 lg 15¹ of the Law of Obligations Act. Finantsinspektsioon may release an institution from the duty, for a term or without one, where its activity and its significance in Estonia justify it. A released institution must tell Finantsinspektsioon when it no longer meets the condition of lg 3 p 3, which concerns the share of payment accounts offered to consumers in all the payment accounts it offers (ten per cent).

titles.en: Securities Market Act

obligations.title: Add the duty: Provide investment services lawfully, with care and in the client's best interests
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Väärtpaberituru seadus (RT I 2001, 89, 532), § 85 lg 1 p 1–3, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 30, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Provide investment services lawfully, with care and in the client's best interests

summaries.en: When providing investment and ancillary services an investment firm must act lawfully and with sufficient expertise, precision and care, putting the client's best interests first. It must have regard to the reliable and orderly functioning of the securities market and follow the act, the rules made under it and its own internal rules.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give or take third-party fees and benefits only where they raise service quality, and keep the evidence
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Väärtpaberituru seadus (RT I 2001, 89, 532), § 85² lg 1–3, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 30, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Give or take third-party fees and benefits only where they raise service quality, and keep the evidence

summaries.en: An investment firm may give to, or receive from, anyone other than the client a monetary or non-monetary fee or benefit in connection with an investment or ancillary service only if it creates no conflict of interest with the client, is designed to enhance the quality of the service to the client and does not impair acting honestly, professionally and in the client's best interests. To prove this it keeps a list of all such fees and benefits and documents how each one enhances the service.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give clients information that is understandable, timely, accurate and complete
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Väärtpaberituru seadus (RT I 2001, 89, 532), § 86 lg 2, 3 ja 6, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 30, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Give clients information that is understandable, timely, accurate and complete

summaries.en: Information an investment firm gives clients and potential clients must be understandable, timely, accurate and complete, and information on the service, the security, its risks and any fees or benefits must let the client understand them and take a considered investment decision. Possible gains may not be stressed without a clear reference to the risks. All information the act requires is given electronically, and a client who is not a professional investor (kutseline investor) may ask for it on paper free of charge.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Assess suitability or appropriateness before providing an investment service
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Väärtpaberituru seadus (RT I 2001, 89, 532), § 87¹ lg 1–3, 11 ja 12, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 30, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Assess suitability or appropriateness before providing an investment service

summaries.en: Before providing an investment service an investment firm must assess whether the service and the security are suitable or appropriate for the client. For investment advice and portfolio management it first obtains the necessary information on the client's knowledge and experience, financial situation including the ability to bear losses, and investment objectives including risk tolerance, and recommends only what fits them; for other services it establishes whether the client has the knowledge and experience needed. It warns the client when the product or service is not appropriate or when the information given does not allow an assessment.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Execute client orders on the best possible terms under a written execution policy
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Väärtpaberituru seadus (RT I 2001, 89, 532), § 87³ lg 1–3 ja 10, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 30, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Execute client orders on the best possible terms under a written execution policy

summaries.en: An investment firm must set and apply legal, technical and organisational measures for the best execution of client orders and lay down its order execution policy in internal rules. It executes each order in the way best for the client, weighing price, costs, speed, likelihood of execution and settlement, size and nature, and follows only the client's instruction where the client has given a specific one. On request it must show the client that the order was executed under the policy, and after execution it tells the client where the order was executed.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep client assets separate, record them per client and have the auditor report each year
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Väärtpaberituru seadus (RT I 2001, 89, 532), § 88 lg 1, 3, 5 ja 7, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 30, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Keep client assets separate, record them per client and have the auditor report each year

summaries.en: An investment firm must keep client assets entrusted to it separate from its own assets and from those of its other clients unless the client has agreed otherwise in a form reproducible on a durable medium, and may use a client's securities in its own interest only with the client's prior express consent. A firm holding client assets on a nominee account or an account in its own name keeps separate records for each client. It lays down its client asset protection principles in internal rules and ensures that Finantsinspektsioon receives, at least once a year, its auditor's report on compliance with them.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Record client orders and conversations and keep the recordings for five years
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Väärtpaberituru seadus (RT I 2001, 89, 532), § 90 lg 1 ja § 90¹ lg 1, 3 ja 6, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 30, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Record client orders and conversations and keep the recordings for five years

summaries.en: An investment firm and the Estonian branch of a foreign investment firm must register and keep the data on the services and transactions provided and on communication with clients. The firm records telephone conversations and electronic communications relating to dealing on own account and to receiving, transmitting and executing client orders, also where no transaction results, and tells clients beforehand that it does so. Recordings are kept for five years, up to seven if Finantsinspektsioon so requires, and given to the client on request.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Set measures against conflicts of interest and disclose those that cannot be prevented
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Väärtpaberituru seadus (RT I 2001, 89, 532), § 82⁴ lg 1, 4 ja 8, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 30, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Set measures against conflicts of interest and disclose those that cannot be prevented

summaries.en: An investment firm must lay down in internal rules, and apply, legal, technical and organisational measures to identify and to prevent or manage conflicts of interest within the firm, with persons controlling it, between the firm and clients and between clients, including those arising from fees and benefits and from the pay of managers and staff. Where the measures do not ensure in a given case that harm to the client's interests is prevented, the firm tells the client the general nature or source of the conflict and the steps taken to mitigate the risks. It does so on a durable medium, before providing the service and in enough detail for the client to take an informed decision.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Run an approval process for every security the firm manufactures for sale
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Väärtpaberituru seadus (RT I 2001, 89, 532), § 82⁹ lg 1, 3, 4 ja 9, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 30, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Run an approval process for every security the firm manufactures for sale

summaries.en: An investment firm that manufactures securities for sale must set in internal rules a process for approving each such security and each significant change to it, and apply it whenever the security is offered or marketed. The structure and features of the security may not harm clients' interests or the reliable and orderly functioning of the market, and before launch the firm assesses that the security threatens neither the market nor financial stability and analyses possible conflicts of interest. The detailed requirements apply as far as is appropriate and proportionate to the security, its target market and the service.

obligations.title: Add the duty: As a listed issuer, publish the annual report within four months and the half-yearly report within three
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Väärtpaberituru seadus (RT I 2001, 89, 532), § 184¹⁰ lg 1 ja § 184¹¹ lg 1, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 30, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: As a listed issuer, publish the annual report within four months and the half-yearly report within three

summaries.en: An issuer whose securities are admitted to trading on a regulated market in Estonia or another EEA state, and whose home state is Estonia, must publish its annual report within four months of the end of the financial year. An issuer of shares or debt securities must publish a half-yearly report on the first six months of the financial year within three months of the end of that period. Each report must stay publicly available for at least ten years, and § 184¹³ exempts certain issuers.

instruments.title: Add MERAS, the Estonian Payment Institutions and E-money Institutions Act (Makseasutuste ja e-raha asutuste seadus)
instruments.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Makseasutuste ja e-raha asutuste seadus (MERAS), RT I 2010, 2, 3, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 53, in force from 01.10.2026 to 30.03.2029, read through the gazette's own interface; entry into force read in the text's header (jõustumine 22.01.2010)

titles.en: Payment Institutions and E-money Institutions Act

payload.officialRef: Makseasutuste ja e-raha asutuste seadus (RT I 2010, 2, 3)
payload.implementsNote: PSD2, Directive (EU) 2015/2366; Second E-Money Directive, Directive 2009/110/EC; Payment Accounts Directive, Directive 2014/92/EU (the directives the act's footnote in Riigi Teataja lists, which also names Regulation (EU) 2024/886 on instant credit transfers)

obligations.title: Add the duty: Set and apply internal rules covering services, ICT security, continuity and incident handling
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Makseasutuste ja e-raha asutuste seadus (RT I 2010, 2, 3), § 50 lg 1–3, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 53, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Set and apply internal rules covering services, ICT security, continuity and incident handling

summaries.en: A payment institution and an e-money institution must set and apply internal rules for the institution, its managers and its employees that ensure compliance with the law and with the decisions of its governing bodies and the lawful and orderly provision of services, and must regularly assess and update them. The rules cover, among other things, information flows, the provision of services with a plan against business interruption, reporting lines and segregation of duties, the security of ICT and client asset systems, internal control, sanctions and anti-money laundering procedures, security complaints and incidents, access to sensitive payment data, business continuity and statistics on performance, transactions and fraud.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep data unchanged and available to Finantsinspektsioon for five years
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Makseasutuste ja e-raha asutuste seadus (RT I 2010, 2, 3), § 51 lg 6 ja 7, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 53, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Keep data unchanged and available to Finantsinspektsioon for five years

summaries.en: A payment institution, an e-money institution and their foreign branches must keep the data the act requires unchanged and available to Finantsinspektsioon for five years, unless Finantsinspektsioon has set another period or a law sets a longer one. Documents setting out the rights, duties and terms under which a client is served are kept for as long as the legal relationship with the client lasts.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Notify payment agents to Finantsinspektsioon and check agents and branches on site once a year
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Makseasutuste ja e-raha asutuste seadus (RT I 2010, 2, 3), § 59 lg 2, 4 ja 5 ja § 51 lg 5¹, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 53, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Notify payment agents to Finantsinspektsioon and check agents and branches on site once a year

summaries.en: A payment institution that intends to provide services through a payment agent must first give Finantsinspektsioon the agent's name, address and managers, its anti-money laundering controls, proof of trustworthiness, the services concerned and its registry or personal identification code, and must report changes and the end of the agency without delay. It must ensure that the agent tells clients on whose behalf it acts. Payment and e-money institutions check that their agents and branches comply and carry out an on-site check at the agent's or branch's place of business at least once a year.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Notify outsourcing in advance and stay fully responsible for outsourced tasks
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Makseasutuste ja e-raha asutuste seadus (RT I 2010, 2, 3), § 62 lg 1, 2, 4, 5 ja 8¹, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 53, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Notify outsourcing in advance and stay fully responsible for outsourced tasks

summaries.en: A payment institution or e-money institution that hands tasks related to its services to a third party must tell Finantsinspektsioon beforehand and report without delay when the arrangement ends or its circumstances change. Important tasks and ICT systems may not be outsourced in a way that impairs internal control or supervision, managers may not delegate their responsibility, and clients' interests and the conditions of the licence may not be affected. The institution sets an outsourcing procedure in its internal rules and stays fully responsible for the outsourced tasks, also where it uses agents or distributors.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Issue e-money at par on receipt of funds and redeem it at par on request
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Makseasutuste ja e-raha asutuste seadus (RT I 2010, 2, 3), § 63 lg 2, 3, 5 ja 6, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 53, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Issue e-money at par on receipt of funds and redeem it at par on request

summaries.en: An e-money issuer must issue e-money without delay at the nominal value of the funds received and must redeem it at nominal value, for cash or a transfer to a payment account, whenever the holder asks. The contract with the holder must state the redemption conditions and any fees clearly, and the issuer tells the client about them before the contract is concluded. A redemption fee must be proportionate to actual costs and may be charged only in the cases the section lists.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Answer payment service complaints within 15 working days
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Makseasutuste ja e-raha asutuste seadus (RT I 2010, 2, 3), § 63¹, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 53, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Answer payment service complaints within 15 working days

summaries.en: A payment service provider must answer a client's complaint in writing or in a form that can be reproduced in writing, and tell the client that the claim is met or how the complaint may be resolved, within a reasonable time and no later than 15 working days after receiving it. Where reasons beyond its control prevent this, it must explain the delay and set a deadline for finishing that may not exceed 35 working days.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Send Finantsinspektsioon an updated operational and security risk assessment by 1 March each year
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Makseasutuste ja e-raha asutuste seadus (RT I 2010, 2, 3), § 63⁵ lg 1 ja 2, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 53, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Send Finantsinspektsioon an updated operational and security risk assessment by 1 March each year

summaries.en: A payment service provider must apply security measures and control mechanisms to manage the operational risks, security risks included, of the payment services it provides. Each year by 1 March, or more often if Finantsinspektsioon so requires, it submits an updated assessment of those risks and of the adequacy of the measures taken in response.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Safeguard client funds by separation or by insurance
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Makseasutuste ja e-raha asutuste seadus (RT I 2010, 2, 3), § 79 lg 1 ja 3 ja § 80 lg 1 ja 3, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 53, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Safeguard client funds by separation or by insurance

summaries.en: A payment institution providing the payment services of § 3 lg 1 p 1–6 must keep client funds received for payment services separate from its own assets and, where they have not been passed on by the end of the working day after receipt, hold them in a separate account with a credit institution or Eesti Pank or invest them in secure, liquid, low-risk instruments. An e-money institution must hold the funds received for issued e-money in the same way. Instead, the funds may be covered by an insurance policy or comparable guarantee from an insurer or credit institution outside the institution's group.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give payment institutions access to payment account services on objective and proportionate terms
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Makseasutuste ja e-raha asutuste seadus (RT I 2010, 2, 3), § 63⁸, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 53, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Give payment institutions access to payment account services on objective and proportionate terms

summaries.en: A credit institution must give payment institutions access to its payment account services on terms that are objective and proportionate and treat them equally, and extensive enough for them to provide payment services to their clients unhindered and efficiently. It must give Finantsinspektsioon the reasons for any refusal of access.

instruments.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Rahapesu ja terrorismi rahastamise tõkestamise seadus (RahaPTS), RT I, 17.11.2017, 2, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 93, in force from 21.07.2026 to 30.03.2029, read through the gazette's own interface; entry into force read in the text's header (jõustumine 27.11.2017)

titles.en: Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Prevention Act

obligations.title: Add the duty: Assess and document the firm's money laundering and terrorist financing risks and its risk appetite
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Rahapesu ja terrorismi rahastamise tõkestamise seadus (RT I, 17.11.2017, 2), § 13 lg 1, 3 ja 4, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 93, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Assess and document the firm's money laundering and terrorist financing risks and its risk appetite

summaries.en: An obliged entity must draw up a risk assessment to identify, assess and analyse the money laundering and terrorist financing risks of its activities, covering at least customer, geographical, product, service or transaction, and delivery channel risks. From it the entity determines its lower and higher risk areas, its risk appetite and its risk management model, including simplified and enhanced due diligence measures. The assessment and the risk appetite are documented, updated as needed and in line with the published national risk assessment, and given to the supervisor on request.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Set rules of procedure and internal control rules approved by senior management
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Rahapesu ja terrorismi rahastamise tõkestamise seadus (RT I, 17.11.2017, 2), § 14 lg 1–3, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 93, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Set rules of procedure and internal control rules approved by senior management

summaries.en: An obliged entity must establish rules of procedure that effectively mitigate and manage the risks found in its risk assessment, and internal control rules for checking that they are followed. The rules of procedure cover at least customer due diligence including the simplified and enhanced measures, a customer risk model and risk profiles, the handling and reporting of suspicions and unusual transactions, record keeping, the identification of politically exposed persons, sanctioned persons and high-risk countries, and the risks of new technologies, products and channels. They are set by senior management, proportionate to the business and regularly checked and updated.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Name the responsible management board member and a contact person agreed with the Financial Intelligence Unit
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Rahapesu ja terrorismi rahastamise tõkestamise seadus (RT I, 17.11.2017, 2), § 17 lg 1, 2, 4 ja 5, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 93, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Name the responsible management board member and a contact person agreed with the Financial Intelligence Unit

summaries.en: An obliged entity with more than one management board member must name the member responsible for applying the act. The management board of a credit institution or financial institution, or the head of a branch, appoints a contact person for the Rahapesu Andmebüroo (the Financial Intelligence Unit) who reports directly to it, works permanently in Estonia and has the competence, means, access to information, suitability and impeccable reputation the role needs. The appointment is agreed with the Rahapesu Andmebüroo and notified to it and to the supervisor.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Apply customer due diligence before a business relationship or occasional transaction
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Rahapesu ja terrorismi rahastamise tõkestamise seadus (RT I, 17.11.2017, 2), § 19 lg 1 ja 5 ja § 20 lg 1, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 93, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Apply customer due diligence before a business relationship or occasional transaction

summaries.en: An obliged entity must apply due diligence measures when establishing a business relationship, when carrying out an occasional transaction of 15,000 euros or more, when it doubts earlier data and whenever it suspects money laundering or terrorist financing. The measures are identifying the customer and verifying the identity from a reliable and independent source, identifying and verifying a representative and the right of representation, identifying the beneficial owner and understanding the ownership and control structure, understanding the purpose of the relationship or transaction, finding out whether a politically exposed person is involved, and monitoring the relationship. The first five are applied before the relationship is established or the transaction carried out.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Monitor business relationships and keep customer data up to date
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Rahapesu ja terrorismi rahastamise tõkestamise seadus (RT I, 17.11.2017, 2), § 23, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 93, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Monitor business relationships and keep customer data up to date

summaries.en: An obliged entity must set principles for monitoring its business relationships. Monitoring includes checking that transactions are consistent with what the entity knows of the customer, its activities and its risk profile, regularly updating the documents and data gathered in due diligence, identifying the source and origin of the funds used, and paying closer attention to complex, high-value and unusual transactions without a reasonable economic or lawful purpose and to customers and payees linked to high-risk third countries.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Apply enhanced due diligence wherever the risk is higher than usual
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Rahapesu ja terrorismi rahastamise tõkestamise seadus (RT I, 17.11.2017, 2), § 36 lg 1–3, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 93, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Apply enhanced due diligence wherever the risk is higher than usual

summaries.en: An obliged entity must apply enhanced due diligence to manage and mitigate a higher than usual risk. It always does so where there are doubts about the data, the documents or the beneficial owner, where the customer is a politically exposed person, where the customer or the payee's payment service provider is from a high-risk third country or from a country without effective anti-money laundering systems or on the EU list of non-cooperative tax jurisdictions, where a crypto-asset transfer goes to or comes from a self-hosted address, and in the other cases the section lists. It also does so where its own risk assessment shows a higher risk.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Obtain senior management approval and establish the source of wealth for politically exposed persons
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Rahapesu ja terrorismi rahastamise tõkestamise seadus (RT I, 17.11.2017, 2), § 41 lg 1 ja 3, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 93, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Obtain senior management approval and establish the source of wealth for politically exposed persons

summaries.en: Where a customer, a person taking part in a transaction or their beneficial owner is a politically exposed person, a family member or a person known to be a close associate, the obliged entity must also obtain senior management approval to establish or continue the relationship, take measures to establish the source of wealth and of the funds used, and monitor the relationship in an enhanced way. After the person stops performing the prominent public function, the entity takes the remaining risk into account for at least 12 months and applies risk-sensitive measures until the specific risk is gone.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Refuse or end a relationship when due diligence cannot be completed or laundering is suspected
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Rahapesu ja terrorismi rahastamise tõkestamise seadus (RT I, 17.11.2017, 2), § 42 lg 1, 2, 4 ja 6, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 93, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Refuse or end a relationship when due diligence cannot be completed or laundering is suspected

summaries.en: An obliged entity may not establish a business relationship or allow a transaction to be made or completed if it cannot apply the due diligence the act requires or if it suspects money laundering or terrorist financing, and may not deal with a person more than 10 per cent of whose capital consists of bearer shares or other bearer securities. Where a relationship exists, a customer's refusal to give the information or documents needed is a material breach, and the entity must terminate the contract without notice and report the customer to the Rahapesu Andmebüroo under § 49. The prohibition does not apply where the entity has reported and received a specific instruction from the Rahapesu Andmebüroo to continue.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep due diligence and transaction records for five years and then delete them
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Rahapesu ja terrorismi rahastamise tõkestamise seadus (RT I, 17.11.2017, 2), § 47 lg 1–4 ja 7, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 93, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Keep due diligence and transaction records for five years and then delete them

summaries.en: An obliged entity must keep the originals or copies of the documents used to identify and verify, the registered data and the documents on which the business relationship rests for five years after the relationship ends, together with all correspondence, monitoring data and data on suspicious or unusual transactions that were not reported. Transaction documents and the material behind a report are kept for at least five years after the transaction or the report. The records must allow a full and immediate answer to enquiries from the Rahapesu Andmebüroo, supervisors, investigators or a court, and are deleted when the period ends unless other law provides otherwise.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report suspicions to the Financial Intelligence Unit within two working days
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Rahapesu ja terrorismi rahastamise tõkestamise seadus (RT I, 17.11.2017, 2), § 49 lg 1–4 ja 6, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 93, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Report suspicions to the Financial Intelligence Unit within two working days

summaries.en: An obliged entity that identifies activity or circumstances pointing to the use of criminal proceeds or to terrorist financing, or that suspects or knows of money laundering or terrorist financing, must report to the Rahapesu Andmebüroo without delay and no later than two working days later, also where the transaction is not carried out. A credit institution also reports within two working days every cash currency exchange above 32,000 euros with a person with whom it has no business relationship, while other obliged entities report every cash transaction above 32,000 euros. The transaction is postponed until the report is made unless postponement could cause substantial harm, is impossible or could hinder catching the offender, and the entity gives the Rahapesu Andmebüroo all the information it asks for without delay.

instruments.title: Add RSanS, the Estonian International Sanctions Act (Rahvusvahelise sanktsiooni seadus)
instruments.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Rahvusvahelise sanktsiooni seadus (RSanS), RT I, 19.03.2019, 11, consolidated text RT I, 17.05.2025, 4, in force from 01.07.2026, read through the gazette's own interface; entry into force read in § 45 of the act

titles.en: International Sanctions Act

obligations.title: Add the duty: Name the management board member and the person responsible for applying financial sanctions
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Rahvusvahelise sanktsiooni seadus (RT I, 19.03.2019, 11), § 20 lg 1–3, consolidated text RT I, 17.05.2025, 4, in force from 01.07.2026

titles.en: Name the management board member and the person responsible for applying financial sanctions

summaries.en: A person with special obligations, which includes every credit institution and financial institution, that has more than one management board member must name the member responsible for meeting the duties of §§ 21–23. It must also appoint a person responsible for performing the tasks of the act, the application of financial sanctions included, and send that person's contact details to the Rahapesu Andmebüroo and to Finantsinspektsioon. The rules on the anti-money laundering contact person apply to that person.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Screen customers whenever a financial sanction enters into force, changes or ends
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Rahvusvahelise sanktsiooni seadus (RT I, 19.03.2019, 11), § 21 lg 1, 1¹ ja 1², consolidated text RT I, 17.05.2025, 4, in force from 01.07.2026

titles.en: Screen customers whenever a financial sanction enters into force, changes or ends

summaries.en: When a financial sanction enters into force, is amended or ends, a person with special obligations must check whether anyone it has or plans a business relationship with is a subject of the sanction, and must update its sanctions lists without delay. To identify sanctioned persons it applies the due diligence measures of the anti-money laundering act when establishing a relationship and monitors the relationship, having regard to its own risks and those of the sanction. If it identifies a sanctioned person or a transaction that breaches the sanction, it applies the sanction and notifies the Rahapesu Andmebüroo without delay.

obligations.title: Add the duty: When in doubt, apply the sanction, gather more information and notify the Financial Intelligence Unit
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Rahvusvahelise sanktsiooni seadus (RT I, 19.03.2019, 11), § 21 lg 2–4, consolidated text RT I, 17.05.2025, 4, in force from 01.07.2026

titles.en: When in doubt, apply the sanction, gather more information and notify the Financial Intelligence Unit

summaries.en: Where a person with special obligations doubts whether a customer is a sanctioned person or whether a transaction or act breaches a financial sanction, or where there is a risk or suspicion of a breach, it applies the sanction and gathers and verifies, from reliable and independent sources, further information on the person and on the purpose and nature of the relationship, transaction or act. If this confirms the doubt or does not settle it, or a breach is suspected, it notifies the Rahapesu Andmebüroo of this and of the sanction applied.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep sanctions screening data for five years after the relationship ends
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Rahvusvahelise sanktsiooni seadus (RT I, 19.03.2019, 11), § 22 lg 1–3, consolidated text RT I, 17.05.2025, 4, in force from 01.07.2026

titles.en: Keep sanctions screening data for five years after the relationship ends

summaries.en: A person with special obligations must collect and keep the data gathered in meeting § 21, or on a suspected or threatened breach of a sanction relating to goods or services, for five years after the business relationship ends, also where no transaction was concluded. The data must allow a full and immediate answer to enquiries from the Rahapesu Andmebüroo, supervisors, investigators or a court. The period runs on while an investigation or court case is pending or the sanction has applied for longer than five years.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Build and document a sanctions risk management system and train staff
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Rahvusvahelise sanktsiooni seadus (RT I, 19.03.2019, 11), § 22¹ lg 2–4, consolidated text RT I, 17.05.2025, 4, in force from 01.07.2026

titles.en: Build and document a sanctions risk management system and train staff

summaries.en: A person with special obligations must set up, on the basis of its risk appetite and risk assessment, a system for mitigating and managing international sanctions risk, document and update it and act on it. The system contains at least a general strategy, the risk appetite and risk assessment, rules of procedure and guidance, due diligence, action in the situations of § 21, data collection and retention, internal control and staff training. Employees who establish business relationships or carry out transactions are trained when they start and regularly or as needed after that.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Set written sanctions procedures and internal control rules
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Rahvusvahelise sanktsiooni seadus (RT I, 19.03.2019, 11), § 23 lg 1–3, consolidated text RT I, 17.05.2025, 4, in force from 01.07.2026

titles.en: Set written sanctions procedures and internal control rules

summaries.en: A person with special obligations must set, in writing or a form reproducible in writing, rules of procedure that give it an organisation able to notice at once when a financial sanction enters into force, changes or ends. They contain guidance at least on identifying sanctioned persons and breaching transactions, acting on suspicion, establishing the risk of a breach, due diligence, notifying the Rahapesu Andmebüroo and keeping data. Internal control rules set the frequency and procedure of checks and how results are kept, and the entity ensures its employees apply both.

obligations.title: Add the duty: File financial sanctions reports with the Financial Intelligence Unit
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Rahvusvahelise sanktsiooni seadus (RT I, 19.03.2019, 11), § 32¹, consolidated text RT I, 17.05.2025, 4, in force from 01.07.2026

titles.en: File financial sanctions reports with the Financial Intelligence Unit

summaries.en: A person with special obligations must submit reports to the Rahapesu Andmebüroo containing information on persons, funds, economic resources, accounts, payments and transactions and other data needed to implement and apply financial sanctions. Unless the legal act imposing or implementing the sanction provides otherwise, a report is required no more often than once a month. The Minister sets the detailed content, the reporting persons and the procedure by regulation.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report suspected breaches of trade and service sanctions to the customs and consumer authorities
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Rahvusvahelise sanktsiooni seadus (RT I, 19.03.2019, 11), § 13³, consolidated text RT I, 17.05.2025, 4, in force from 01.07.2026

titles.en: Report suspected breaches of trade and service sanctions to the customs and consumer authorities

summaries.en: A credit institution must notify the Maksu- ja Tolliamet (Tax and Customs Board) of a suspicion or risk that a sanction banning the import or export of goods is breached, and the Tarbijakaitse ja Tehnilise Järelevalve Amet (Consumer Protection and Technical Regulatory Authority) of a suspicion or risk that a sanction relating to a service is breached. It passes on the data it has learned, personal data included, and answers those authorities' enquiries.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Send the securities register the citizenships of securities account holders with a non-EEA citizenship
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Rahvusvahelise sanktsiooni seadus (RT I, 19.03.2019, 11), § 22², consolidated text RT I, 17.05.2025, 4, in force from 01.07.2026

titles.en: Send the securities register the citizenships of securities account holders with a non-EEA citizenship

summaries.en: Where a natural person holding a securities account is not a citizen of Estonia, another EU or EEA state or Switzerland, or holds another citizenship besides one of those, a credit institution must send the Estonian register of securities all the citizenships it knows of. For a holder with none of those citizenships it also sends what it knows about a residence permit and its expiry and the other data the act requires. On the register's request it sends other data needed to apply a sanction that it collected in anti-money laundering due diligence.

instruments.title: Add IFS, the Estonian Investment Funds Act (Investeerimisfondide seadus)
instruments.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Investeerimisfondide seadus (IFS), RT I, 31.12.2016, 3, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 70, in force from 21.07.2026, read through the gazette's own interface; entry into force read in the text's header (jõustumine 10.01.2017)

titles.en: Investment Funds Act

payload.implementsNote: UCITS Directive, Directive 2009/65/EC, with Commission Directives 2007/16/EC, 2010/43/EU and 2010/44/EU and Delegated Directive (EU) 2021/1270; IORP II, Directive (EU) 2016/2341; Directive (EU) 2019/1160 on the cross-border distribution of funds (the directives the act's footnote in Riigi Teataja lists)

obligations.title: Add the duty: Act in the best interests of the fund and its investors
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Investeerimisfondide seadus (RT I, 31.12.2016, 3), § 340 lg 2, 4 ja 7, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 70, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Act in the best interests of the fund and its investors

summaries.en: A management company must act in the best interests of the fund and its investors. When investing fund assets it obtains sufficient information on the assets it intends to buy or has bought and monitors the financial position of the issuers and counterparties concerned. It reports information pointing to a breach of law, harm to investors' interests or a breach of the requirements for the fund to Finantsinspektsioon and to the depositary, and remedies the defect without delay.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Set internal rules and keep internal audit, compliance and risk control working
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Investeerimisfondide seadus (RT I, 31.12.2016, 3), § 340 lg 1 ja § 344 lg 1–3, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 70, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Set internal rules and keep internal audit, compliance and risk control working

summaries.en: A management company must establish and apply the internal rules its business needs and ensure that the internal audit, compliance and risk control functions work effectively, also where they are outsourced. The rules must be adequate and proportionate and ensure compliance with the law, with the decisions of its governing bodies and with the fund's rules, articles or prospectus. They cover, among other things, information flows, segregation of duties, ICT and business continuity in line with DORA, internal control and risk management, conflicts of interest and personal transactions, remuneration, delegation, complaints, valuation, record keeping, and sanctions and anti-money laundering procedures.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Run a conflicts of interest procedure, disclose unmanaged conflicts and keep a register
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Investeerimisfondide seadus (RT I, 31.12.2016, 3), § 351 lg 1, 6 ja 7, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 70, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Run a conflicts of interest procedure, disclose unmanaged conflicts and keep a register

summaries.en: A management company must establish and apply a procedure with legal, technical and organisational measures to identify, manage and where possible prevent conflicts of interest in managing funds: within the company, with those controlling it, between funds and investors and between investors and its other clients. Where the measures do not prevent the risk of harm in a particular case, it tells the fund's investors the general nature or source of the conflict before the transaction. It keeps and regularly updates a register of conflicts that carry a material risk of harming investors.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Have the supervisory board approve the remuneration principles and review them every year
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Investeerimisfondide seadus (RT I, 31.12.2016, 3), § 354 lg 1–3, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 70, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Have the supervisory board approve the remuneration principles and review them every year

summaries.en: The supervisory board of a management company must approve, and review at least once a year, the principles for the pay and benefits of management board members and employees; the decision and its oversight rest with members who hold no other management role and know risk management and remuneration. The principles must be clear, transparent and consistent with sound risk management, must not encourage risk-taking at odds with the funds' documents and investment policy, and must contain measures against conflicts of interest. Internal control checks their application at least once a year unless there is a remuneration committee.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Handle investor complaints promptly and free of charge and keep a record
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Investeerimisfondide seadus (RT I, 31.12.2016, 3), § 360, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 70, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Handle investor complaints promptly and free of charge and keep a record

summaries.en: A management company must set in its internal rules a procedure for handling investors' complaints promptly and free of charge, which lets an investor complain in the official language of the state where the UCITS is established or its units are publicly offered. Information on the procedure is made available to investors free of charge. The company registers every complaint and keeps the data on the measures taken to resolve it.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Delegate tasks only under the statutory conditions and notify Finantsinspektsioon at once
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Investeerimisfondide seadus (RT I, 31.12.2016, 3), § 364 lg 1, 3 ja 4, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 70, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Delegate tasks only under the statutory conditions and notify Finantsinspektsioon at once

summaries.en: A management company may delegate its activities to a third party only by written contract and only if this does not harm the fund or its investors, hinder the company's work or its supervision, or leave the company no longer managing the fund, and if the delegate is qualified, reputable, experienced, bound to follow instructions and open to the company's checks. The company must be able to justify the delegation and show that the delegate was chosen with due care. It notifies Finantsinspektsioon without delay, submitting the contract, and remains liable for the management of the fund.

obligations.title: Add the duty: File quarterly supervisory reports within 25 days and the annual report by 1 May
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Investeerimisfondide seadus (RT I, 31.12.2016, 3), § 370 lg 1–4 ja 6, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 70, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: File quarterly supervisory reports within 25 days and the annual report by 1 May

summaries.en: A management company must draw up and submit supervisory reports to Finantsinspektsioon for each quarter, within 25 days of the end of the period. It submits its annual report, the auditor's report, the profit distribution proposal and decision and the extract of the general meeting's minutes within two weeks of the general meeting and no later than 1 May of the following year, unless they are published on its own or its group's website. The source documents behind the reports are kept for at least five years.

obligations.title: Add the duty: As depositary, hold the fund's assets and check the management company's compliance
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Investeerimisfondide seadus (RT I, 31.12.2016, 3), § 285 lg 1 ja § 289 lg 1 ja 2, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 70, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: As depositary, hold the fund's assets and check the management company's compliance

summaries.en: Every fund must have a depositary, except funds managed by a small fund manager and non-public funds managed by a UCITS management company. The depositary holds the fund's securities and other financial instruments that can be held in custody and keeps records of the remaining assets, settles the fund's transactions, sees that the net asset value is calculated and income distributed under the law and the fund's documents, and carries out the management company's instructions after checking that they comply. It periodically checks that the management company acts in line with the law, the fund's founding document and its internal rules.

instruments.title: Add KindlTS, the Estonian Insurance Activities Act (Kindlustustegevuse seadus)
instruments.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Kindlustustegevuse seadus (KindlTS), RT I, 07.07.2015, 1, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 140, in force from 21.07.2026, read through the gazette's own interface; entry into force read in § 287 of the act

titles.en: Insurance Activities Act

payload.implementsNote: Solvency II, Directive 2009/138/EC; IDD, Directive (EU) 2016/97; Directive 2004/113/EC on equal treatment in goods and services; Directive 2011/89/EU; Omnibus II, Directive 2014/51/EU; IORP II, Directive (EU) 2016/2341; Motor Insurance Directive, Directive 2009/103/EC (the directives the act's footnote in Riigi Teataja lists)

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep an effective system of governance with four key functions and a responsible person for each
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Kindlustustegevuse seadus (RT I, 07.07.2015, 1), § 96 lg 1–3, 5 ja 7, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 140, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Keep an effective system of governance with four key functions and a responsible person for each

summaries.en: An insurance undertaking must have an effective system of governance, proportionate to the nature, scale and complexity of its business, with a transparent organisational structure, proper segregation of duties and a clear allocation of responsibilities. The system must enable it to perform the risk management, actuarial, compliance and internal audit functions, and the undertaking names a person responsible for each key function. It must ensure the continuity and regularity of its activities, contingency plans included.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Assess own risks and solvency regularly and after any significant change in risk profile
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Kindlustustegevuse seadus (RT I, 07.07.2015, 1), § 100 lg 1, 2 ja 4, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 140, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Assess own risks and solvency regularly and after any significant change in risk profile

summaries.en: As part of its risk management system an insurance undertaking must assess its overall solvency needs in the light of its risk profile, approved risk tolerance limits and business strategy, its continuous compliance with the capital requirements and the rules on technical provisions, and how far its risk profile deviates from the assumptions behind the Solvency Capital Requirement. It sets proportionate procedures that let it identify and assess short and long term risks. The assessment is made regularly and without delay after any significant change in the risk profile.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Name a person who ensures distribution staff are fit, and give them 15 hours of training a year
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Kindlustustegevuse seadus (RT I, 07.07.2015, 1), § 103¹ lg 1 ja 2, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 140, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Name a person who ensures distribution staff are fit, and give them 15 hours of training a year

summaries.en: An insurance undertaking must appoint a person whose task is to ensure that employees directly engaged in insurance distribution, the manager responsible for distribution and natural-person insurance agents are suitable for their work and meet its requirements, and to keep the related records up to date. The undertaking ensures that its distribution employees, its natural-person agents and the distribution staff of agencies whose main business is insurance distribution receive 15 hours of insurance training a year.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Apply a product approval process with a target market and prepare the non-life product information document
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Kindlustustegevuse seadus (RT I, 07.07.2015, 1), § 103² lg 3–6, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 140, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Apply a product approval process with a target market and prepare the non-life product information document

summaries.en: Each time before an insurance product is first offered to its target market or significantly changed, an insurance undertaking must apply its procedure for developing products, proportionately to the nature of the product. It regularly monitors whether the product still meets the needs of the target market and whether the distribution strategy is still appropriate, and makes information on the product and its target market available to all distributors. A manufacturer of a non-life product draws up the insurance product information document under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1469.

obligations.title: Add the duty: As an insurance intermediary, act on the customer's insurable interest and pay staff without conflict
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Kindlustustegevuse seadus (RT I, 07.07.2015, 1), § 177 lg 1 ja 2, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 140, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: As an insurance intermediary, act on the customer's insurable interest and pay staff without conflict

summaries.en: An insurance intermediary must act on the basis of the customer's insurable interest and the requirements of the law, with the care that the complexity of the contract calls for and the foresight and competence expected of an intermediary. The remuneration principles for the natural persons who distribute insurance on its behalf, their targets and assessment criteria included, must not endanger the duty to act in the customer's interest or lead the intermediary to recommend a contract that does not match the customer's insurable interest and demands.

obligations.title: Add the duty: As an insurance agent, identify the customer's needs and give the required information before each contract
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Kindlustustegevuse seadus (RT I, 07.07.2015, 1), § 198 lg 2, 2¹ ja 4, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 140, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: As an insurance agent, identify the customer's needs and give the required information before each contract

summaries.en: In good time before each insurance contract is concluded, and where needed before it is amended, an insurance agent must tell the customer its business name and contact details, that it acts for the insurance undertaking, where its entry in the list of intermediaries can be checked, which contracts it distributes and the extent of its authority. On the customer's information it establishes the customer's insurable interest and demands, recommends the contract that best meets them and explains it so that the customer can decide in an informed way. It also discloses its commission and the basis of its pay, the complaints procedure and any conflict of interest, and for non-life insurance hands over the product information document; none of this applies to the contracts named in § 427 lg 2 and 3 of the Law of Obligations Act.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Establish the customer's insurance needs, recommend the best matching contract and explain it
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Kindlustustegevuse seadus (RT I, 07.07.2015, 1), § 221, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 140, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Establish the customer's insurance needs, recommend the best matching contract and explain it

summaries.en: Each time before an insurance contract is concluded, and where a need is apparent before it is amended, an insurance undertaking must establish from the customer's information the customer's insurable interest and demands, recommend from its own range the contract that best meets them, and give explanations adequate to the complexity of the contract and the type of customer. It must give the person wishing to conclude a contract the information required by the act and by the Law of Obligations Act, before the contract and during it, in the form that act prescribes. The first duty does not apply to contracts concluded through an insurance broker or to the contracts named in § 427 lg 2 and 3 of the Law of Obligations Act.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Assess suitability or appropriateness before concluding life insurance with investment risk
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Kindlustustegevuse seadus (RT I, 07.07.2015, 1), § 222 lg 2–5 ja 10, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 140, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Assess suitability or appropriateness before concluding life insurance with investment risk

summaries.en: Before concluding a life insurance contract with investment risk, an insurance undertaking that gives a recommendation must assess whether the contract and its underlying assets are suitable for the policyholder, gathering information on knowledge and experience in investing, financial capacity and investment objectives. Where no recommendation is given it assesses appropriateness from the policyholder's knowledge and experience, and warns the policyholder if the contract appears inappropriate or the information is insufficient. It documents the assessment and keeps the record until claims under the contract are time-barred.

instruments.title: Add TFS, the Estonian Guarantee Fund Act (Tagatisfondi seadus)
instruments.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Tagatisfondi seadus (TFS), RT I 2002, 23, 131, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 95, in force from 21.07.2026, read through the gazette's own interface; entry into force read in § 117 of the act

titles.en: Guarantee Fund Act

payload.implementsNote: DGSD, Directive 2014/49/EU (the directive the act's footnote in Riigi Teataja lists)

obligations.title: Add the duty: Tell depositors about deposit guarantee cover at the contract and at least once a year
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Tagatisfondi seadus (RT I 2002, 23, 131), § 31 lg 1–1², consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 95, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Tell depositors about deposit guarantee cover at the contract and at least once a year

summaries.en: A credit institution must inform depositors of the extent of the deposit guarantee and of the conditions and procedure for compensation, including the deposits that are not guaranteed. The information is given when the deposit contract is concluded, in the way § 711 lg 2 and 5 of the Law of Obligations Act prescribe, and at least once a year while the contract lasts. The Minister sets the content of the depositor information sheet by regulation.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Tell depositors at least a month before a merger or conversion into a branch
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Tagatisfondi seadus (RT I 2002, 23, 131), § 31 lg 1³, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 95, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Tell depositors at least a month before a merger or conversion into a branch

summaries.en: When credit institutions merge, a subsidiary is converted into a branch or a similar operation takes place, depositors must be informed at least one month before it takes effect. A shorter period is possible only where Finantsinspektsioon or the foreign competent authority has agreed to it on grounds of business secrecy or financial stability.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Pay the regular contribution to the deposit guarantee sub-fund at least once a year
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Tagatisfondi seadus (RT I 2002, 23, 131), § 34 lg 1 ja 4, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 95, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Pay the regular contribution to the deposit guarantee sub-fund at least once a year

summaries.en: A credit institution or branch covered by the deposit guarantee sub-fund pays the regular contribution regularly and at least once a year. If the supervisory board of the Tagatisfond so decides, irrevocable payment commitments that are freely disposable and fully backed by unencumbered low-risk assets may be accepted as contributions, for no more than 30 per cent of the contributions the institution owes in a calendar year.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Do not advertise with the deposit guarantee or the investor protection cover
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Tagatisfondi seadus (RT I 2002, 23, 131), § 31 lg 2 ja § 49 lg 2, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 95, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Do not advertise with the deposit guarantee or the investor protection cover

summaries.en: A credit institution may not use the deposit guarantee under the act for advertising purposes, and an investment institution may not use the investor protection cover for advertising purposes.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Tell investors about the investor protection scheme and its limits
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Tagatisfondi seadus (RT I 2002, 23, 131), § 49 lg 1, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 95, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Tell investors about the investor protection scheme and its limits

summaries.en: An investment institution (an investment firm, a credit institution, or a management company allowed to manage portfolios or hold fund units for clients) must inform investors that the investor protection scheme exists, how far investments are guaranteed and on what conditions and by what procedure compensation is paid.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Pay the regular contribution to the resolution sub-fund and supply the data for calculating it
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Tagatisfondi seadus (RT I 2002, 23, 131), § 73¹⁷ lg 1–3 ja § 73¹⁸ lg 1, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 95, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Pay the regular contribution to the resolution sub-fund and supply the data for calculating it

summaries.en: A credit institution pays the regular contribution to the resolution sub-fund regularly and at least once a year. The contribution is proportionate to its liabilities, less own funds and guaranteed deposits, relative to the same total for all credit institutions, and the Fund may require a third party it accepts to secure the payment. The institution gives the Fund the data needed to calculate the contribution in the way set under § 92 lg 2.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report to the Guarantee Fund through Finantsinspektsioon
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Tagatisfondi seadus (RT I 2002, 23, 131), § 92 lg 2, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 95, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Report to the Guarantee Fund through Finantsinspektsioon

summaries.en: Fund participants must submit reports to the Tagatisfond through Finantsinspektsioon on the deposit guarantee, investor protection, pension protection, pension contract and resolution sub-funds, to the extent and in the way the Minister has set by regulation.

instruments.title: Add FELS, the Estonian recovery and resolution act (Finantskriisi ennetamise ja lahendamise seadus)
instruments.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Finantskriisi ennetamise ja lahendamise seadus (FELS), RT I, 19.03.2015, 3, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 139, in force from 21.07.2026, read through the gazette's own interface; entry into force read in the text's header (jõustumine 29.03.2015)

titles.en: Financial Crisis Prevention and Resolution Act

payload.officialRef: Finantskriisi ennetamise ja lahendamise seadus (RT I, 19.03.2015, 3)
payload.implementsNote: BRRD, Directive 2014/59/EU, as amended up to Directive (EU) 2024/1174 (the directive the act's footnote in Riigi Teataja lists)

obligations.title: Add the duty: Draw up a recovery plan, have both boards approve it and review it at least once a year
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Finantskriisi ennetamise ja lahendamise seadus (RT I, 19.03.2015, 3), § 10 lg 1–6, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 139, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Draw up a recovery plan, have both boards approve it and review it at least once a year

summaries.en: A credit institution, which in this act includes an investment firm subject to the capital requirement of § 93 lg 1 p 1 of the Securities Market Act, must draw up a recovery plan setting out the measures it would take to restore its financial position after a significant deterioration, and submit it to Finantsinspektsioon; a parent in Estonia does so for the whole group. An Estonian subsidiary of a group whose parent is established in another EEA state needs no plan of its own unless it is directly supervised by the European Central Bank, its assets exceed 30 billion euros, its assets exceed 20 per cent of Estonia's gross domestic product and are not below 5 billion euros, or Finantsinspektsioon requires one. The management board approves the plan and the supervisory board confirms it before submission, and the plan is reviewed at least once a year and after any change or event that may materially affect it.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Meet the minimum requirement for own funds and eligible liabilities at all times
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Finantskriisi ennetamise ja lahendamise seadus (RT I, 19.03.2015, 3), § 17 lg 1, 2, 2¹, 3, 7 ja 7², consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 139, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Meet the minimum requirement for own funds and eligible liabilities at all times

summaries.en: A credit institution must at all times meet the minimum requirement for own funds and eligible liabilities that Finantsinspektsioon sets for it, calculated as the sum of own funds and eligible liabilities and expressed as a percentage. Liabilities count only if they meet the conditions of Articles 72a to 72c of the CRR that the section names. Liabilities for which the institution has not included the contractual recognition term of § 22 are left out, and Finantsinspektsioon exempts mortgage credit institutions that fund themselves with covered bonds and may not take deposits, on the conditions of lg 3.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Write bail-in recognition into contracts governed by third-country law
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Finantskriisi ennetamise ja lahendamise seadus (RT I, 19.03.2015, 3), § 22 lg 1, 2¹ ja 3, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 139, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Write bail-in recognition into contracts governed by third-country law

summaries.en: In a contract creating a liability governed by the law of a third country, a credit institution or a member of its group must agree that the creditor or counterparty recognises that the liability may be written down or converted and accepts any reduction, conversion or cancellation in resolution. This does not apply to deposits ranking first in bankruptcy, to liabilities excluded from bail-in by § 71 lg 1, or where third-country law or a treaty already provides for the power. If the institution finds the term legally or otherwise impracticable for a liability, it notifies Finantsinspektsioon with the class of liability and its reasons.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report on the minimum requirement every six months and publish the key figures once a year
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Finantskriisi ennetamise ja lahendamise seadus (RT I, 19.03.2015, 3), § 22¹ lg 1, 2 ja 4, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 139, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Report on the minimum requirement every six months and publish the key figures once a year

summaries.en: A credit institution must report to Finantsinspektsioon on meeting the minimum requirement: the amounts of own funds and eligible liabilities at least once every six months, and the amount of bail-inable liabilities and the composition, maturity profile and insolvency ranking of those amounts at least once a year, unless Finantsinspektsioon requires more frequent reports. At least once a year it publishes on its website the amounts of own funds and eligible liabilities, their composition, maturity profile and ranking, and the requirement that applies to it.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Write recognition of resolution stays into financial contracts governed by third-country law
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Finantskriisi ennetamise ja lahendamise seadus (RT I, 19.03.2015, 3), § 22² lg 1–4, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 139, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Write recognition of resolution stays into financial contracts governed by third-country law

summaries.en: In every financial contract governed by the law of a third country, a credit institution or a member of its group must agree that the counterparty accepts that Finantsinspektsioon may suspend obligations or restrict rights under the contract in resolution, and recognises that it is bound by Article 68 of the BRRD. The duty covers contracts that create a new obligation or materially amend an existing one. The parent of a credit institution operating in the EU must ensure that its third-country subsidiaries put the same terms into their financial contracts, which Finantsinspektsioon may apply to subsidiaries that are credit institutions, investment firms or financial institutions.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Help Finantsinspektsioon draw up the resolution plan and report changes that affect it
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Finantskriisi ennetamise ja lahendamise seadus (RT I, 19.03.2015, 3), § 28 lg 5 ja 7, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 139, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Help Finantsinspektsioon draw up the resolution plan and report changes that affect it

summaries.en: At Finantsinspektsioon's request a credit institution or a member of its group must assist in drawing up and updating the resolution plan and supply the information needed to prepare and apply it, such as its group structure, critical functions and core business lines, liabilities and sources of liquidity. The institution or the group parent notifies Finantsinspektsioon without delay of any change in legal status, organisational structure, business or financial position that may call for the plan to be reviewed.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Tell Finantsinspektsioon when the institution is failing or likely to fail
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Finantskriisi ennetamise ja lahendamise seadus (RT I, 19.03.2015, 3), § 49 lg 1, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 139, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Tell Finantsinspektsioon when the institution is failing or likely to fail
