summaries.en: The management board of a credit institution, or of a member of its group, must notify Finantsinspektsioon when the institution or that member is failing or likely to fail within the meaning of § 39 lg 2.

instruments.title: Add KAVS, the Estonian act on consumer creditors and credit intermediaries (Krediidiandjate ja -vahendajate seadus)
instruments.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krediidiandjate ja -vahendajate seadus (KAVS), RT I, 19.03.2015, 4, consolidated text RT I, 20.06.2026, 24, in force from 30.06.2026 to 30.06.2028, read through the gazette's own interface; entry into force read in the text's header (jõustumine 29.03.2015)

titles.en: Creditors and Credit Intermediaries Act

payload.implementsNote: Mortgage Credit Directive, Directive 2014/17/EU (the directive the act's footnote in Riigi Teataja lists)

obligations.title: Add the duty: Do not tie the pay of credit assessors and advisers to the number of loans approved
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krediidiandjate ja -vahendajate seadus (RT I, 19.03.2015, 4), § 43 lg 1, 3 ja 4, consolidated text RT I, 20.06.2026, 24, in force from 30.06.2026

titles.en: Do not tie the pay of credit assessors and advisers to the number of loans approved

summaries.en: The remuneration principles of a creditor or credit intermediary must be clear, transparent, consistent with sound risk management and its long-term interests, and take account of consumers' legitimate interests. They must contain measures against conflicts of interest: the pay of the management board member or employee responsible for assessing a consumer's creditworthiness may not depend on the number or share of applications approved or contracts concluded. Where advisory services are provided, the pay of the staff concerned may not limit their ability to act in the consumer's interest or be contingent on the number of credit agreements or on sales targets.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Avoid unfair commercial practices and identify the consumer before granting credit
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krediidiandjate ja -vahendajate seadus (RT I, 19.03.2015, 4), § 47 lg 1–3, consolidated text RT I, 20.06.2026, 24, in force from 30.06.2026

titles.en: Avoid unfair commercial practices and identify the consumer before granting credit

summaries.en: When granting or brokering credit to a consumer, a creditor or credit intermediary must avoid unfair commercial practices, give the explanations and information the Law of Obligations Act requires, and meet the creditworthiness assessment and other responsible lending requirements. It must identify the consumer and any representative and verify the information given. Its relations with clients rest on contracts in written, reproducible or electronic form, and it keeps and uses data on the consumer's financial obligations and payment record to assess creditworthiness.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep credit documents for the whole relationship and three years after it ends
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krediidiandjate ja -vahendajate seadus (RT I, 19.03.2015, 4), § 47 lg 5, consolidated text RT I, 20.06.2026, 24, in force from 30.06.2026

titles.en: Keep credit documents for the whole relationship and three years after it ends

summaries.en: A creditor or credit intermediary must keep all the data and documents on granting and servicing a credit, the credit file included, unchanged and available to Finantsinspektsioon for as long as the legal relationship with the consumer lasts and for three years after the relationship or contract ends, unless a legal act provides otherwise.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep a credit file for each consumer
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krediidiandjate ja -vahendajate seadus (RT I, 19.03.2015, 4), § 48 lg 1, 3 ja 5, consolidated text RT I, 20.06.2026, 24, in force from 30.06.2026

titles.en: Keep a credit file for each consumer

summaries.en: A creditor or credit intermediary must keep a credit file, separately for each consumer, of the data and documents gathered to assess creditworthiness, and ensure that what is needed for that analysis is in the file for the whole credit period. The file contains at least the consumer's data, the applications, the decisions to grant or refuse, the contract performance documents, the results of the creditworthiness analysis, the credit and collateral agreements, correspondence, amendments and the documents checking the underlying data. A mortgage creditor or intermediary also files the documents on the checking, insurance and valuation of the property.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Assess creditworthiness under a set methodology and lend only when satisfied the consumer can repay
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krediidiandjate ja -vahendajate seadus (RT I, 19.03.2015, 4), § 49 lg 1, 2, 4 ja 6, consolidated text RT I, 20.06.2026, 24, in force from 30.06.2026

titles.en: Assess creditworthiness under a set methodology and lend only when satisfied the consumer can repay

summaries.en: To meet the responsible lending requirement a creditor or credit intermediary must set in its internal rules a methodology for assessing a consumer's creditworthiness and checking the data, which takes account at least of assets and regular income, other obligations, past payment behaviour, household expenses, the effect of a possible rise in obligations and the terms of the credit. A creditor's rules also set loan-to-value and debt service-to-income ratios, a maximum term and a method for testing the consumer's ability to pay if interest rates change. Credit may be granted only when the analysis has satisfied the creditor that the obligations will be met as agreed, and the consumer must be told of the possible dangers of borrowing.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Verify the income and obligations the consumer declares
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krediidiandjate ja -vahendajate seadus (RT I, 19.03.2015, 4), § 50 lg 1, 3 ja 4, consolidated text RT I, 20.06.2026, 24, in force from 30.06.2026

titles.en: Verify the income and obligations the consumer declares

summaries.en: A creditor or credit intermediary obtains the information needed to assess creditworthiness from the consumer, from relevant internal sources and from databases, and must make reasonable efforts to verify what the consumer has said, relying where possible on information it can obtain independently. Where the other information is not enough, it checks the consumer's income and obligations against a credit institution account statement supplied by the consumer where possible.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give personalised mortgage credit advice only on proper information and in the consumer's interest
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krediidiandjate ja -vahendajate seadus (RT I, 19.03.2015, 4), § 51 lg 1, 2, 6 ja 7, consolidated text RT I, 20.06.2026, 24, in force from 30.06.2026

titles.en: Give personalised mortgage credit advice only on proper information and in the consumer's interest

summaries.en: A mortgage creditor or intermediary must tell the consumer whether advisory services are or can be provided. When advising, a creditor or its agent considers a sufficient number of the creditor's own suitable agreements and an intermediary considers suitable agreements on the market, and the consumer receives a personalised recommendation on a durable medium that suits the consumer's financial situation and purposes. Before advising, the provider states on a durable medium whether the recommendation rests on one or several creditors' products and what the advice costs, gathers data on the consumer's situation, preferences and objectives, and acts in the consumer's interest.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Value residential collateral independently of the credit decision and keep the valuation for three years
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krediidiandjate ja -vahendajate seadus (RT I, 19.03.2015, 4), § 53 lg 1–3, consolidated text RT I, 20.06.2026, 24, in force from 30.06.2026

titles.en: Value residential collateral independently of the credit decision and keep the valuation for three years

summaries.en: A creditor offering residential property credit to consumers must set requirements for the property it accepts as security and the terms for establishing the mortgage. The valuation must be independent enough of the credit decision to be objective and impartial, and whoever values the property, an employee or a third party, must have sufficient knowledge, experience and skills. The valuation is documented on a durable medium and the documents are kept unchanged and available to Finantsinspektsioon for at least three years after the contract with the consumer ends.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep general information on residential property credit available to consumers at all times
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krediidiandjate ja -vahendajate seadus (RT I, 19.03.2015, 4), § 53¹ lg 1 ja 2, consolidated text RT I, 20.06.2026, 24, in force from 30.06.2026

titles.en: Keep general information on residential property credit available to consumers at all times

summaries.en: A creditor and a credit agent must make clear and understandable general information on residential property credit agreements available to consumers at all times, on a durable medium or electronically. It states at least who the creditor or intermediary is, the purposes of the credit, the forms of security, the possible duration, the types of interest rate and any benchmark, foreign currency risks, a representative example with the total cost and the annual percentage rate of charge, other costs, repayment options, early repayment terms, valuation, tied ancillary contracts and a warning about the consequences of default.

instruments.title: Add VÕS, the Estonian Law of Obligations Act, for its consumer credit and payment services rules
instruments.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Võlaõigusseadus (VÕS), RT I 2001, 81, 487, consolidated text RT I, 20.06.2026, 18, in force from 01.09.2026 to 31.12.2026, read through the gazette's own interface; entry into force read in the text's header (jõustumine 01.07.2002)

titles.en: Law of Obligations Act

payload.implementsNote: Among the directives the act's footnote in Riigi Teataja lists: Mortgage Credit Directive, Directive 2014/17/EU; Commission Directive 2011/90/EU amending the annex to the Consumer Credit Directive; Payment Accounts Directive, Directive 2014/92/EU; Financial Collateral Directive, Directive 2002/47/EC; IDD, Directive (EU) 2016/97; Consumer Rights Directive, Directive 2011/83/EU

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give the consumer the Standard European Consumer Credit Information form before the credit agreement
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Võlaõigusseadus (RT I 2001, 81, 487), § 403¹ lg 1, 2 ja 6, consolidated text RT I, 20.06.2026, 18, in force from 01.09.2026

titles.en: Give the consumer the Standard European Consumer Credit Information form before the credit agreement

summaries.en: So that the consumer can compare offers, a creditor or credit intermediary must give the consumer, in good time before the consumer is bound by a contract or offer and on a durable medium, the Standard European Consumer Credit Information form with the data the section lists, among them the type and amount of credit, the duration, the repayments, the total amount payable, the borrowing rate, the annual percentage rate of charge, default charges, the right of withdrawal and the right of early repayment. On request the consumer also receives a free copy of the draft agreement. Residential property credit has its own pre-contract information rule in § 403³.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Assess the consumer's creditworthiness and conclude the agreement only if the consumer can repay
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Võlaõigusseadus (RT I 2001, 81, 487), § 403⁴ lg 1, 2, 6, 7 ja 9, consolidated text RT I, 20.06.2026, 18, in force from 01.09.2026

titles.en: Assess the consumer's creditworthiness and conclude the agreement only if the consumer can repay

summaries.en: Before concluding a consumer credit agreement a creditor must obtain the information needed to judge whether the consumer can repay on the agreed terms and assess that creditworthiness with due care, taking account of assets, regular income, other obligations, past payment behaviour and the effect of a possible rise in obligations. It may conclude the agreement only if the analysis has satisfied it that the consumer is creditworthy, and it reassesses before any increase of the amount or limit. If it concludes the agreement without being so satisfied, the interest falls to the statutory rate of § 94 where that is lower and the consumer owes no other charges.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Explain the credit so the consumer can judge whether it fits their needs and finances
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Võlaõigusseadus (RT I 2001, 81, 487), § 403⁵ lg 1 ja 2, consolidated text RT I, 20.06.2026, 18, in force from 01.09.2026

titles.en: Explain the credit so the consumer can judge whether it fits their needs and finances

summaries.en: Before a consumer credit agreement is concluded, a creditor or credit intermediary must give the consumer adequate explanations so that the consumer can assess whether the proposed agreement suits their needs and financial situation; for residential property credit this extends to any ancillary contract offered. Where the consumer can be expected to need or want more, it must explain further the pre-contract information, the main features of the products and their effects, including the consequences of late payment, and warn of the possible dangers of taking credit.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep the annual percentage rate of charge within three times the published average
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Võlaõigusseadus (RT I 2001, 81, 487), § 406² lg 1 ja 3, consolidated text RT I, 20.06.2026, 18, in force from 01.09.2026

titles.en: Keep the annual percentage rate of charge within three times the published average

summaries.en: A consumer credit agreement is void if the annual percentage rate of charge payable by the consumer is more than three times the average rate for consumer loans granted by credit institutions to private individuals over the last six months, as last published by Eesti Pank when the credit is granted. Under a void agreement the consumer repays what was received by the original final due date with interest only at the statutory rate of § 94 lg 1, and the creditor must recalculate the repayments and tell the consumer.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Terminate an instalment credit for default only after three missed instalments and two weeks' notice
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Võlaõigusseadus (RT I 2001, 81, 487), § 416 lg 1 ja 2, consolidated text RT I, 20.06.2026, 18, in force from 01.09.2026

titles.en: Terminate an instalment credit for default only after three missed instalments and two weeks' notice

summaries.en: A creditor may terminate a consumer credit repayable in instalments for the consumer's default only if the consumer is wholly or partly in arrears with at least three consecutive repayments and the creditor has without success given at least two further weeks to pay the shortfall, stating that it will otherwise terminate and demand the whole debt. The notice of termination must be in a form reproducible in writing or it is void. No later than when setting the additional period the creditor must offer the consumer the possibility of negotiating an agreement.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Open a basic payment account for any consumer lawfully resident in the EU within ten business days
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Võlaõigusseadus (RT I 2001, 81, 487), § 710¹ lg 2, 4, 6 ja 8, consolidated text RT I, 20.06.2026, 18, in force from 01.09.2026

titles.en: Open a basic payment account for any consumer lawfully resident in the EU within ten business days

summaries.en: Unless the law provides otherwise, a credit institution must provide basic payment services to a consumer lawfully resident in the European Union and conclude a contract for them where the consumer has a justified interest, through several channels including an internet application. It must conclude the contract or tell the consumer of a refusal without delay and within ten business days of a proper application, and give the refusal and its reasons in writing and free of charge unless disclosure would conflict with national security, public order or the anti-money laundering act. It may not make the contract conditional on buying additional services.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give each consumer a statement of fees at least once a year, free of charge
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Võlaõigusseadus (RT I 2001, 81, 487), § 718¹ lg 1–3, consolidated text RT I, 20.06.2026, 18, in force from 01.09.2026

titles.en: Give each consumer a statement of fees at least once a year, free of charge

summaries.en: A payment service provider must give a consumer, at least once a year and free of charge, a statement of all fees charged for the services on the list of the most representative payment account services, with the overdraft and deposit interest rates where they apply. The means of communication is agreed with the consumer, who may ask for the statement on paper or another durable medium. It shows at least the unit fee and number of uses of each service, the total charged per service, the interest charged and earned, and the total of all fees.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Apply strong customer authentication to online account access and electronic payments
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Võlaõigusseadus (RT I 2001, 81, 487), § 724⁶ lg 1, 3 ja 4, consolidated text RT I, 20.06.2026, 18, in force from 01.09.2026

titles.en: Apply strong customer authentication to online account access and electronic payments

summaries.en: A payment service provider must use secure communication for authentication and apply security measures that protect the confidentiality and integrity of personalised security credentials. It requires strong customer authentication whenever the payer accesses the payment account online, initiates an electronic payment transaction or carries out any remote action that carries a risk of payment fraud or other abuse, unless the law provides otherwise. For electronic payments initiated remotely, the authentication includes elements that dynamically link the transaction to a specific amount and payee.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Credit the payee's provider by the end of the next business day
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Võlaõigusseadus (RT I 2001, 81, 487), § 728 lg 1, 2, 4 ja 6, consolidated text RT I, 20.06.2026, 18, in force from 01.09.2026

titles.en: Credit the payee's provider by the end of the next business day

summaries.en: The payer's payment service provider must ensure that the amount reaches the account of the payee's provider no later than the business day after the payment order is received, with one more business day allowed for paper-initiated orders. The payee's provider makes the amount available to the payee without delay once it has been credited to the provider's account. Cash a consumer pays into an account in the account's currency must be available immediately after receipt.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Refund an unauthorised payment by the end of the next business day
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Võlaõigusseadus (RT I 2001, 81, 487), § 733² lg 1, 2 ja 4, consolidated text RT I, 20.06.2026, 18, in force from 01.09.2026

titles.en: Refund an unauthorised payment by the end of the next business day

summaries.en: For an unauthorised payment the payer's payment service provider may claim neither fees nor expenses from the payer and must refund the amount without delay, and no later than the business day after learning of the payment, restoring the account to the state it would have been in, with the debit date as value date. It may refuse the refund only in a case of fraud by the payer, and only if it reports the possible fraud to the police.

instruments.title: Add IKS, the Estonian Personal Data Protection Act (Isikuandmete kaitse seadus)
instruments.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Isikuandmete kaitse seadus (IKS), RT I, 04.01.2019, 11, consolidated text RT I, 30.06.2026, 52, in force from 01.10.2026, read through the gazette's own interface; entry into force read in § 76 of the act

titles.en: Personal Data Protection Act

payload.implementsNote: Supplements the GDPR, Regulation (EU) 2016/679, and transposes the Law Enforcement Directive, Directive (EU) 2016/680, as § 1 of the act states; the act's footnote in Riigi Teataja lists the directive

obligations.title: Add the duty: Pass on payment default data only for credit assessment, after checking and logging it
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Isikuandmete kaitse seadus (RT I, 04.01.2019, 11), § 10, consolidated text RT I, 30.06.2026, 52, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Pass on payment default data only for credit assessment, after checking and logging it

summaries.en: Personal data on a breach of an obligation may be passed to a third party, and processed by that party, only to assess the data subject's creditworthiness or for a similar purpose, and only if the controller or processor has checked that the data are accurate and that there is a legal basis for the transfer, and has registered the transfer. Collection and transfer are not allowed for special categories of personal data, for data on offences before the public hearing or decision, where they would excessively harm the data subject, within 30 days of the breach of contract, or more than five years after the breach has ended.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Rely on a child's consent for online services only from the age of 13
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Isikuandmete kaitse seadus (RT I, 04.01.2019, 11), § 8, consolidated text RT I, 30.06.2026, 52, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Rely on a child's consent for online services only from the age of 13

summaries.en: Where consent under Article 6(1)(a) of the GDPR is the basis for offering information society services directly to a child, the child's personal data may be processed only if the child is at least 13 years old. For a younger child, processing is allowed only if and as far as the child's legal representative has consented.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Apply the ten-year rule to the personal data of deceased persons
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Isikuandmete kaitse seadus (RT I, 04.01.2019, 11), § 9, consolidated text RT I, 30.06.2026, 52, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Apply the ten-year rule to the personal data of deceased persons

summaries.en: A data subject's consent stays valid during their lifetime and for ten years after their death, or 20 years where the person died a minor, unless the data subject decided otherwise. After the death, personal data may be processed with the consent of any one heir; that consent is not needed once those periods have passed, where another legal basis applies, or where only the name, sex, dates of birth and death, the fact of death and the time and place of burial are processed.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Notify people when recording sound or images in a public place for publication
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Isikuandmete kaitse seadus (RT I, 04.01.2019, 11), § 11, consolidated text RT I, 30.06.2026, 52, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Notify people when recording sound or images in a public place for publication

summaries.en: Unless a law provides otherwise, when sound or images are recorded in a public place in order to be made public, the data subject's consent is replaced by notifying them in a way that lets them understand that recording is taking place and avoid it if they wish. The duty to notify does not apply to public events where recording for publication can reasonably be expected.

instruments.title: Add MTVS, the Estonian act on the exchange of tax information (financial accounts, FATCA, cross-border arrangements and crypto-assets)
instruments.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Maksualase teabevahetuse seadus (MTVS), RT I, 23.12.2014, 15, consolidated text RT I, 15.04.2026, 2, in force from 25.04.2026 to 30.12.2027, read through the gazette's own interface; entry into force read in § 29 of the act

titles.en: Tax Information Exchange Act

payload.implementsNote: DAC, Directive 2011/16/EU, as amended up to DAC8, Directive (EU) 2023/2226, with DAC2, Directive 2014/107/EU, and DAC6, Directive (EU) 2018/822; Directive (EU) 2021/2101 on public country-by-country reporting (the directives the act's footnote in Riigi Teataja lists)

obligations.title: Add the duty: Tell each client at onboarding that tax information is collected and exchanged automatically
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Maksualase teabevahetuse seadus (RT I, 23.12.2014, 15), § 6 lg 2, consolidated text RT I, 15.04.2026, 2, in force from 25.04.2026

titles.en: Tell each client at onboarding that tax information is collected and exchanged automatically

summaries.en: When establishing a business relationship within the meaning of the anti-money laundering act, a reporting entity (teabeandja) must inform the client, in a form reproducible in writing, of the collection of information, the exchange of information and the automatic transmission of information under the act. The duty does not bind an entity that has no obligation to submit the collected information to the tax authority.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep evidence of compliance for the current and six preceding years
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Maksualase teabevahetuse seadus (RT I, 23.12.2014, 15), § 8 lg 3, consolidated text RT I, 15.04.2026, 2, in force from 25.04.2026

titles.en: Keep evidence of compliance for the current and six preceding years

summaries.en: A reporting entity must keep the evidence showing that it has met its duties under the act for at least the current and the six preceding calendar years, but for no longer than ten years, having regard to the purpose limitation principle of the GDPR.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Send corrected information as soon as an error in a report is found
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Maksualase teabevahetuse seadus (RT I, 23.12.2014, 15), § 8 lg 4 ja § 6 lg 4, consolidated text RT I, 15.04.2026, 2, in force from 25.04.2026

titles.en: Send corrected information as soon as an error in a report is found

summaries.en: Where a reporting entity finds that information it sent to the tax authority for the current or the five preceding calendar years is incorrect for a reason attributable to it, it must submit updated information at the first opportunity. The same applies where the data subject proves such an error.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Identify reportable financial accounts each year and report them by 30 June
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Maksualase teabevahetuse seadus (RT I, 23.12.2014, 15), § 8⁶, consolidated text RT I, 15.04.2026, 2, in force from 25.04.2026

titles.en: Identify reportable financial accounts each year and report them by 30 June

summaries.en: A reporting Estonian financial institution must apply the reporting and due diligence rules of Annexes I and II of Directive 2011/16/EU and identify each year the tax information on the financial accounts it maintains. It reports the data of non-resident account holders, and of entities and their non-resident controlling persons, where they are reportable persons resident for tax purposes in a jurisdiction on the list published by the Maksu- ja Tolliamet. The information for the previous calendar year is filed with the tax authority by electronic return by 30 June each year, and the institution must refrain from anything aimed at avoiding the collection of the information.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Collect FATCA data on US accounts and file the return by 30 June
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Maksualase teabevahetuse seadus (RT I, 23.12.2014, 15), § 16 lg 1, 2 ja 5 ja § 18 lg 1, consolidated text RT I, 15.04.2026, 2, in force from 25.04.2026

titles.en: Collect FATCA data on US accounts and file the return by 30 June

summaries.en: A reporting Estonian financial institution must collect, for each year, the data named in Article 2(2)(a) of the FATCA agreement with the United States, applying the due diligence procedures of Annex I to the agreement. The data for a calendar year are collected and filed electronically with the tax authority by 30 June of the following year.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Register with the US Internal Revenue Service without delay
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Maksualase teabevahetuse seadus (RT I, 23.12.2014, 15), § 17, consolidated text RT I, 15.04.2026, 2, in force from 25.04.2026

titles.en: Register with the US Internal Revenue Service without delay

summaries.en: A reporting Estonian financial institution must register without delay with the Internal Revenue Service of the United States and meet the registration requirements of Article 4(1)(c) of the FATCA agreement. Where it fits the conditions of points (d) and (e) of that paragraph it must meet those requirements as well.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report cross-border tax arrangements within 30 calendar days
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Maksualase teabevahetuse seadus (RT I, 23.12.2014, 15), § 20¹⁰ lg 1–2 ja § 20¹³ lg 1–3, consolidated text RT I, 15.04.2026, 2, in force from 25.04.2026

titles.en: Report cross-border tax arrangements within 30 calendar days

summaries.en: An intermediary (a person who designs, markets, makes available or manages the implementation of a reportable cross-border arrangement, or who knowingly gives aid, assistance or advice on one) must report to the tax authority the information it knows on the arrangement, including who the intermediaries and relevant taxpayers are, the hallmarks met, a summary of the arrangement, its start date, legal details, value and the member states concerned. The report is due within 30 calendar days from the day after the arrangement is made available or is ready for implementation, or from the first step of implementation, whichever comes first. For marketable arrangements new information is reported every three months.

obligations.title: Add the duty: As a crypto-asset service provider, identify reportable users and report their transactions by 30 June
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Maksualase teabevahetuse seadus (RT I, 23.12.2014, 15), § 8¹⁵ lg 1–3 ja § 23⁸ lg 2, consolidated text RT I, 15.04.2026, 2, in force from 25.04.2026

titles.en: As a crypto-asset service provider, identify reportable users and report their transactions by 30 June

summaries.en: A reporting Estonian crypto-asset service provider must identify reportable transactions and reportable crypto-asset users under the reporting and due diligence rules of Annex VI of Directive 2011/16/EU and refrain from anything aimed at avoiding this. It files the information for the previous calendar year with the tax authority by electronic return by 30 June each year. The rules are applied for the first time to information for 2026, with the first report due by 30 June 2027.

instruments.title: Add FIS, the Estonian act on the Financial Supervision Authority, for the fees supervised firms pay
instruments.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Finantsinspektsiooni seadus (FIS), RT I 2001, 48, 267, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 12, in force from 01.10.2026 to 30.12.2038, read through the gazette's own interface; entry into force read in § 66 lg 1 of the act (the text's header gives 01.01.2002, the day § 66 lg 2 names for part of the act)

titles.en: Financial Supervision Authority Act

payload.implementsNote: Financial Conglomerates Directive, Directive 2002/87/EC; CRD, Directive 2013/36/EU; Omnibus I, Directive 2010/78/EU; Commission Implementing Directive (EU) 2015/2392; IDD, Directive (EU) 2016/97; IORP II, Directive (EU) 2016/2341; Directive (EU) 2019/2177; MiFID II, Directive 2014/65/EU; Directive (EU) 2019/879; CER Directive, Directive (EU) 2022/2557; Directive (EU) 2022/2381 (the directives the act's footnote lists; read in the XML of the text, because the plain text leaves the footnote out)

obligations.title: Add the duty: Pay the supervision fee to Finantsinspektsioon
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Finantsinspektsiooni seadus (RT I 2001, 48, 267), § 38 lg 1–5 ja 7, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 12, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Pay the supervision fee to Finantsinspektsioon

summaries.en: Credit institutions, insurers, investment firms, payment and e-money institutions, creditors, management companies, crypto-asset service providers and the other supervised firms the section lists must pay a supervision fee made up of a capital share and a volume share. Insurance brokers, credit intermediaries and Estonian branches of foreign firms pay the volume share only. The duty starts when the decision giving the right to operate takes effect and ends when that right ends, and a firm active in several fields pays as one supervised firm.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Pay the supervision fee's capital share and advance by 31 December and the balance by 1 September
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Finantsinspektsiooni seadus (RT I 2001, 48, 267), § 43 lg 2 ja 10 ja § 44, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 12, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Pay the supervision fee's capital share and advance by 31 December and the balance by 1 September

summaries.en: The supervision fee is paid as an advance and a final payment into Finantsinspektsioon's account. The capital share and the advance on the volume share for a budget year are paid by 31 December of the preceding year, and the final payment of the volume share by 1 September of the budget year. Where the duty to pay arises during a year, the capital share is paid within 30 days.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give Finantsinspektsioon the data it asks for to calculate the supervision fee
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Finantsinspektsiooni seadus (RT I 2001, 48, 267), § 38 lg 10, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 12, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Give Finantsinspektsioon the data it asks for to calculate the supervision fee

summaries.en: A firm that owes the supervision fee must give Finantsinspektsioon the additional data, documents and written explanations it requires for calculating the fee.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Pay the processing fee before filing an application with Finantsinspektsioon
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Finantsinspektsiooni seadus (RT I 2001, 48, 267), § 45¹, § 45² ja § 45¹⁰, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 12, in force from 01.10.2026

titles.en: Pay the processing fee before filing an application with Finantsinspektsioon

summaries.en: A person who asks Finantsinspektsioon to review an application or carry out an act for which the act sets a processing fee, such as a licence application or the approval of a prospectus or of fund rules, must pay the fee into Finantsinspektsioon's account before submitting the application or before the act is carried out. The payment document names the act paid for, or the provision under which the fee is paid, and the person on whose behalf it is paid.

instruments.title: Add PandiKS, the Estonian Covered Bonds Act (Pandikirjaseadus)
instruments.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Pandikirjaseadus (PandiKS), RT I, 28.02.2019, 1, consolidated text RT I, 13.02.2026, 12, in force from 01.03.2026, read through the gazette's own interface; entry into force read in § 76 of the act

titles.en: Covered Bonds Act

payload.implementsNote: Covered Bond Directive, Directive (EU) 2019/2162 (the directive the act's footnote in Riigi Teataja lists)

obligations.title: Add the duty: Hold a banking licence and an additional licence before issuing covered bonds
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Pandikirjaseadus (RT I, 28.02.2019, 1), § 3 lg 1, 2 ja 5, consolidated text RT I, 13.02.2026, 12, in force from 01.03.2026

titles.en: Hold a banking licence and an additional licence before issuing covered bonds

summaries.en: To issue covered bonds a company needs both the credit institution licence of § 13 of the Credit Institutions Act and an additional licence for issuing covered bonds, which Finantsinspektsioon grants to companies entered in the Estonian commercial register. When the additional licence ends the credit institution may issue no new covered bonds.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep a cover register for each type of covered bond and preserve its data for ten years
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Pandikirjaseadus (RT I, 28.02.2019, 1), § 11 lg 1, 2 ja 7, consolidated text RT I, 13.02.2026, 12, in force from 01.03.2026

titles.en: Keep a cover register for each type of covered bond and preserve its data for ten years

summaries.en: An issuer must keep a cover register separately for mortgage covered bonds and for covered bonds with a mixed cover pool, in which the cover assets the act requires are recorded; its entries decide what belongs to the cover pool. The register consists of a main register and sub-registers that show all the cover assets and derivatives of each covered bond portfolio. The issuer ensures the recorded data are preserved and can be reproduced while a claim is in the register and for ten years after it is removed.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Appoint an independent cover pool monitor and file the engagement contract within three working days
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Pandikirjaseadus (RT I, 28.02.2019, 1), § 12 lg 1, 3 ja 4, consolidated text RT I, 13.02.2026, 12, in force from 01.03.2026

titles.en: Appoint an independent cover pool monitor and file the engagement contract within three working days

summaries.en: An issuer must appoint an independent cover pool monitor to perform the tasks the act sets. The monitor is an audit firm that ensures the work is done only by a trustworthy sworn auditor of impeccable business reputation with sufficient knowledge and experience, and may not be the firm that audits the issuer or did so in the year before the appointment. The client contract with the monitor is submitted to Finantsinspektsioon within three working days of signing.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep covered bonds covered at all times with at least five per cent overcollateralisation
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Pandikirjaseadus (RT I, 28.02.2019, 1), § 18 lg 1, 6 ja 7, consolidated text RT I, 13.02.2026, 12, in force from 01.03.2026

titles.en: Keep covered bonds covered at all times with at least five per cent overcollateralisation

summaries.en: The principal of all outstanding covered bonds of one type, the interest due on them, the net liabilities under derivatives entered in the cover register and the expected costs of managing the portfolio in a wind-down must at all times be covered by cover assets whose nominal value exceeds the covered liabilities by at least five per cent. The issuer ensures this through calculation models set in its internal rules and documented clearly, which is a task of its managers. Cover assets may not be sold, encumbered or removed from the register if the cover pool or the liquidity buffer would fall below the required level.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Hold a liquidity buffer for the largest net outflow of the next 180 days, at least two per cent of the cover pool
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Pandikirjaseadus (RT I, 28.02.2019, 1), § 21 lg 3 ja 5–7, consolidated text RT I, 13.02.2026, 12, in force from 01.03.2026

titles.en: Hold a liquidity buffer for the largest net outflow of the next 180 days, at least two per cent of the cover pool

summaries.en: To secure the liquidity of the covered bond portfolio, the issuer calculates every day, for each of the next 180 days, the difference between payments due under the covered bonds and registered derivatives and the cash flows coming in from the cover assets, and adds the daily differences up. The largest negative cumulative result must at all times be covered by the liquid assets the section allows, and the buffer must in any case be at least two per cent of the nominal value of the cover pool. The buffer is part of the cover pool and is entered in a separate sub-register.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Stress test the covered bond portfolio at least every three months
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Pandikirjaseadus (RT I, 28.02.2019, 1), § 22 lg 1 ja 2, consolidated text RT I, 13.02.2026, 12, in force from 01.03.2026

titles.en: Stress test the covered bond portfolio at least every three months

summaries.en: At least once every three months an issuer must stress test each covered bond portfolio to assess the risks named in its methodology and to check the value of the cover pool; seeing that the tests take place is a task of the issuer's managers. If the cover pool value calculated in the test does not meet the coverage requirements, the issuer adds cover assets to the register for the largest shortfall found, or secures the shortfall in another form.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Count mortgage loans as cover only up to 70 per cent of the property's value
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Pandikirjaseadus (RT I, 28.02.2019, 1), § 26, consolidated text RT I, 13.02.2026, 12, in force from 01.03.2026

titles.en: Count mortgage loans as cover only up to 70 per cent of the property's value

summaries.en: An issuer's claims under a mortgage credit may be used as cover for mortgage covered bonds only up to 70 per cent of the value of the property securing the credit, although every registered mortgage claim belongs to the cover pool in full. The property must carry a mortgage of an amount of at least 110 per cent of the credit granted.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Publish cover pool information every quarter and keep five years of it on the website
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Pandikirjaseadus (RT I, 28.02.2019, 1), § 55 lg 1–4, consolidated text RT I, 13.02.2026, 12, in force from 01.03.2026

titles.en: Publish cover pool information every quarter and keep five years of it on the website

summaries.en: An issuer must publish information on its covered bond portfolios once a quarter: for the first three quarters within 20 days of the end of the quarter and for the fourth within two months. The published information must stay available on the issuer's website for at least the last five years. The section lists the data to be published for each type of covered bond.

instruments.title: Add KrüTS, the Estonian act supplementing MiCA (Krüptovaraturu seadus)
instruments.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krüptovaraturu seadus (KrüTS), RT I, 21.06.2024, 3, original text RT I, 21.06.2024, 3, in force from 01.07.2024, read through the gazette's own interface; entry into force read in the header of the act's first and only version (Redaktsiooni jõustumise kp: 01.07.2024)

titles.en: Crypto-asset Market Act

payload.implementsNote: Supplements MiCA, Regulation (EU) 2023/1114, and DORA, Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, as § 1 of the act states

obligations.title: Add the duty: Hold a crypto-asset market licence or Finantsinspektsioon's confirmation before operating
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krüptovaraturu seadus (RT I, 21.06.2024, 3), § 5 lg 1 ja 4 ja § 6 lg 1, original text RT I, 21.06.2024, 3, in force from 01.07.2024

titles.en: Hold a crypto-asset market licence or Finantsinspektsioon's confirmation before operating

summaries.en: A crypto-asset market participant (a crypto-asset service provider, an issuer of asset-referenced tokens, e-money tokens or other crypto-assets, or an offeror or person seeking admission to trading) needs a licence from Finantsinspektsioon to operate, unless § 6 or MiCA provides otherwise, and a licensed participant must have its registered office in Estonia. A credit institution, e-money institution, investment firm, UCITS or alternative fund manager, central securities depository or market operator may act as a crypto-asset service provider once Finantsinspektsioon has confirmed by decision that it meets Article 60 of MiCA and has given complete information.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Operate as a limited company with a supervisory board and at least two management board members
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krüptovaraturu seadus (RT I, 21.06.2024, 3), § 7 lg 1–3, original text RT I, 21.06.2024, 3, in force from 01.07.2024

titles.en: Operate as a limited company with a supervisory board and at least two management board members

summaries.en: A crypto-asset market participant may operate only as a private or public limited company. A private limited company must have a supervisory board of at least three members, except a crypto-asset service provider that does not provide the services of Article 3(1)(16)(a) or (b) of MiCA, and the management board of a crypto-asset service provider has at least two members. Under § 2 lg 2 these rules do not apply to credit institutions and the other regulated firms named there.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Notify changes in the management body 30 days before a new member starts
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krüptovaraturu seadus (RT I, 21.06.2024, 3), § 7 lg 6, original text RT I, 21.06.2024, 3, in force from 01.07.2024

titles.en: Notify changes in the management body 30 days before a new member starts

summaries.en: An issuer of asset-referenced tokens and a crypto-asset service provider must notify Finantsinspektsioon, in line with Article 33 or 69 of MiCA, of a change in the management body at least 30 days before the new member starts work, unless notice by then is impossible for a compelling reason. Under § 2 lg 2 this does not apply to credit institutions and the other regulated firms named there.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Ensure staff who advise or inform on crypto-assets have the knowledge and skills listed
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krüptovaraturu seadus (RT I, 21.06.2024, 3), § 8 lg 1, original text RT I, 21.06.2024, 3, in force from 01.07.2024

titles.en: Ensure staff who advise or inform on crypto-assets have the knowledge and skills listed

summaries.en: A crypto-asset service provider must ensure that anyone who gives advice or information on crypto-assets or crypto-asset services on its behalf has the necessary knowledge and skills. They include understanding the services, the types of crypto-asset and their risks, best execution under Article 78 of MiCA, conflicts of interest, data protection, complaints handling and dispute resolution, market abuse prevention, anti-money laundering rules, and the parties' rights, costs and withdrawal and termination terms.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report major ICT incidents to Finantsinspektsioon and the Information System Authority
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krüptovaraturu seadus (RT I, 21.06.2024, 3), § 9 lg 1–3, original text RT I, 21.06.2024, 3, in force from 01.07.2024

titles.en: Report major ICT incidents to Finantsinspektsioon and the Information System Authority

summaries.en: A crypto-asset service provider and an issuer of asset-referenced tokens must meet the digital operational resilience requirements of DORA, Regulation (EU) 2022/2554. They report a major ICT-related incident to Finantsinspektsioon and to the Riigi Infosüsteemi Amet (Information System Authority) under Article 19 of DORA, using the notification templates and time limits set under Article 20 unless technical reasons prevent using the template for the initial notification. Under § 2 lg 2 the section does not apply to credit institutions and the other regulated firms named there.

obligations.title: Add the duty: File the annual report within six months and regular supervisory reports within 20 days
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Krüptovaraturu seadus (RT I, 21.06.2024, 3), § 15 lg 1–3 ja 5, original text RT I, 21.06.2024, 3, in force from 01.07.2024

titles.en: File the annual report within six months and regular supervisory reports within 20 days

summaries.en: A crypto-asset market participant must submit its annual report, the profit distribution proposal and decision and the extract of the minutes approving the report to Finantsinspektsioon within two weeks of the general or shareholders' meeting and no later than six months after the financial year ends, unless it has published them on its website, where they must stay for at least five years, or filed the audited report with the commercial register in time. Regular supervisory reports cover a quarter or a year and are due within 20 days of the end of the period unless otherwise provided. Of these rules only those on supervisory reports apply to the credit institutions and other regulated firms named in § 2 lg 2.

instruments.title: Add EVKS, the Estonian act on the maintenance of the register of securities (Väärtpaberite registri pidamise seadus)
instruments.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Väärtpaberite registri pidamise seadus (EVKS), RT I 2000, 57, 373, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 101, in force from 21.07.2026, read through the gazette's own interface; entry into force read in § 88 of the act

titles.en: Securities Register Maintenance Act

payload.implementsNote: Shareholder Rights Directive, Directive 2007/36/EC (the directive the act's footnote in Riigi Teataja lists)

obligations.title: Add the duty: As account operator, send register data on time and protect it against unauthorised processing
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Väärtpaberite registri pidamise seadus (RT I 2000, 57, 373), § 1⁴ lg 2 ja 3, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 101, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: As account operator, send register data on time and protect it against unauthorised processing

summaries.en: An account operator must ensure that the data needed for register acts reach the registrar in time and that acts concerning securities accounts are carried out within its competence in line with the act and the registrar's rules. It must protect the data it sends to the registrar and stores in connection with a securities account, by administrative, physical, software and hardware measures, against unauthorised processing, including use, destruction and alteration.

obligations.title: Add the duty: As nominee account holder, keep records that identify each client and their securities
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Väärtpaberite registri pidamise seadus (RT I 2000, 57, 373), § 6 lg 3, 5, 9 ja 10, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 101, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: As nominee account holder, keep records that identify each client and their securities

summaries.en: The holder of a nominee account may hold on it only securities held for and on behalf of clients, and must keep records that allow each client to be identified and each client's securities and their number to be determined. The records show the data the act lists on every person on whose order it acquired securities, except where the holder is an EEA credit institution, investment firm or management company entitled to hold client securities in its own name, whose records follow the law of the EEA state where they are kept. Where it holds clients' money in a payment account in its own name in connection with the nominee account, it keeps a record of the money held for each client and disposes of it only on the client's instructions.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give a listed issuer the identity of the shareholders behind a nominee account without delay
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Väärtpaberite registri pidamise seadus (RT I 2000, 57, 373), § 6 lg 9²–9⁴, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 101, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Give a listed issuer the identity of the shareholders behind a nominee account without delay

summaries.en: At the request of an issuer of shares admitted to trading on a regulated market, or of a third party it names, the holder of a nominee account must give without delay the data on the shareholders on whose order it acquired the shares. The information may be sent through the registrar's account operator and follows the format of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/1212.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Verify the identity and authority of anyone giving a register order
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Väärtpaberite registri pidamise seadus (RT I 2000, 57, 373), § 34 lg 1–3, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 101, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Verify the identity and authority of anyone giving a register order

summaries.en: An account operator may carry out orders and enquiries only from persons entitled to dispose of the securities registered on the account, and must identify the person giving the order or asking for register data and verify that person's identity and rights. It must carry out the lawful orders of the account holder, a bailiff, a trustee in bankruptcy and, in the cases the act names, a pledgee. It may not send the registrar an order without a corresponding instruction from the account holder or a duly authorised person, unless a law provides otherwise.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Check the data sent to the registrar and keep order documents for ten years
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Väärtpaberite registri pidamise seadus (RT I 2000, 57, 373), § 34 lg 4 ja 6, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 101, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: Check the data sent to the registrar and keep order documents for ten years

summaries.en: An account operator must check the accuracy of the data it sends to the registrar and is liable to the account holder, the authorised person and the registrar for the correctness of the orders it sends and for their matching the will of the person who gave them. It must keep the documents underlying every order for register acts and enquiries for ten years from the day the order was given.

obligations.title: Add the duty: As an issuer, tell the registrar at once of corporate events and changes in securities' terms
obligations.sourceLabel: Riigi Teataja, Väärtpaberite registri pidamise seadus (RT I 2000, 57, 373), § 21 lg 2–4, consolidated text RT I, 11.07.2026, 101, in force from 21.07.2026

titles.en: As an issuer, tell the registrar at once of corporate events and changes in securities' terms

summaries.en: An issuer must notify the registrar without delay of changes in the rights and obligations of holders of its registered securities, a decision to pay a dividend, interest and redemption payments on debt, a merger, division, transformation, liquidation or bankruptcy, the convening of a general meeting where its securities are traded on a regulated market or multilateral trading facility, and changes in who may represent it before the registrar. Where the issuer sets a record date, the application and data for the register entries must reach the registrar at least five working days before it.
